question: A team is deciding whether to implement a customer-issue resolution system as a fixed workflow or as an autonomous agent. Which of the following characteristics of the task support choosing an autonomous agent architecture over a predefined workflow?
options: A) The steps required to resolve every issue are identical and can be fully specified as a fixed sequence well in advance
B) The number and order of steps needed to resolve an issue cannot be known until the model inspects the specific case
C) The task's cases vary widely enough that hardcoding every possible path in advance would be impractical
D) The team needs the lowest possible latency and cost for every single resolution the system produces
E) The team can fully enumerate every possible resolution path before the system processes a real case
F) The task requires tight, real-time feedback loops so the model can adjust its next action based on tool results
correct_answers: B) The number and order of steps needed to resolve an issue cannot be known until the model inspects the specific case
C) The task's cases vary widely enough that hardcoding every possible path in advance would be impractical
F) The task requires tight, real-time feedback loops so the model can adjust its next action based on tool results
explanations: Incorrect. Identical, fully specifiable steps across every case are exactly the condition under which a predefined workflow is preferred over an agent.
Correct. Steps that can only be determined at runtime by inspecting the specific case are a hallmark reason to favor an autonomous agent over a predefined workflow.
Correct. When case variability makes it impractical to hardcode every path, an autonomous agent's dynamic decision-making becomes the more suitable choice.
Incorrect. Autonomous agents generally incur higher latency and cost than fixed workflows due to their iterative, exploratory nature, so this need points toward a workflow instead.
Incorrect. The ability to fully enumerate every path in advance is a signal that a fixed workflow, not an autonomous agent, is the appropriate choice.
Correct. Autonomous agents are built for tasks requiring tight feedback loops where the model adapts its next action based on tool results, unlike fixed workflows.
